qc_saint_andre_de_kamouraska.blurb: Saint-André-de-Kamouraska is a river-and-sea-side climbing site in Quebec's Bas-Saint-Laurent region, with walls, blocks and overhangs set against the water. Sport routes dominate, backed by a good number of top-rope lines, a few trad routes and a small set of boulder problems. Grades start in the easy range and reach 5.12, but the weight sits between 5.10 and 5.12, with a modest spread of 5.6 to 5.9 routes for newer leaders. The rock is quartzite, described as soft yet compact. The main cliff is L'Amphitheatre, and Parc de la Madone is the separate bouldering park.

wi_high_cliff_state_park.blurb: High Cliff State Park sits on the Niagara Escarpment above the shore of Lake Winnebago in Calumet County, Wisconsin, near Appleton, with woodland on the level ground above the bluff. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, joined by top-rope lines and a smaller number of trad routes. Boulder problems run from V0 to V8 but cluster between V1 and V4, while roped climbs span 5.4 to 5.12 with a fair number between 5.9 and 5.11. The park splits into North Side, West Side and South Side. The main cliff is short, faces west, and has cracks and ledges, with top-rope anchors set in trees above. Early-season rain can leave the cracks wet and muddy.

wy_shady_side.blurb: Shady Side is a sport-climbing zone in Sinks Canyon near Lander, Wyoming, and it lives up to the name by sitting in shade for most of the day, which makes it a summer destination. Every route is sport. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12 and a modest group of easier lines. The crags include Aspen Grade Wall, the tall cliff with long climbs, where winter is described as cold, plus Heavy Metal Rock Band, The School, which is the easiest area and sees heavy use, and Porter's Prow with a few 5.11 routes.

ak_grapefruit_rocks.blurb: Grapefruit Rocks is a limestone climbing area north of Fairbanks, Alaska, reached by the Elliott Highway. It sits on low domes and rolling hills of boreal forest, with birch and aspen groves and black and white spruce. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a solid supply of top-rope and trad lines and a handful of boulder problems. Grades run from 5.4 to 5.13, but most fall between 5.9 and 5.11, so intermediate climbers have the most to choose from. The limestone is polished, with thin edges that reward precise footwork. The rock splits into East Grapefruit Rocks and West Grapefruit Rocks. Long daylight and big temperature swings shape the experience.
